notes:
Very little has been written on these verses one at a time. Most commentators handle 6:54–81 as a single block that repeats Joshua 21, so several verses get only a note on a place name. Some things I couldn't find at all: no Catholic or Orthodox notes on this passage, no netbible.org or bibleodyssey.org notes, no teaching from the prosperity, word‑of‑faith or hyper‑grace camps, and no clear disagreement between Protestant traditions. The one real difference of opinion I found is about whether the cities of refuge are a picture of Christ (see "Cities of refuge" below). I had no information to add for Heshbon and Jazer (v. 81).

**About the whole section (vv. 54–81)**

- **Same list as Joshua 21.** Ellicott says this list covers the same ground as Joshua 21:3–40 and upon the whole, it is in substantial agreement. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **How the list is ordered.** The Pulpit Commentary describes the order: the priestly Kohathites first, then the Gershomites and the Merarites; then the same three families again for the members who were not priests (vv. 66–81). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **Why the Chronicler included it.** The Pulpit Commentary says these references were designed to confirm their claim for reinstatement in their properties on the return from the Captivity. Same URL. Bible Hub's chapter summary agrees: Chronicles repeats the list to reassure post-exilic Levites that the promise still stands. https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm
- **Why the Levites were spread out.**
  - Matthew Henry gives three reasons: it fulfilled Jacob's prediction that Levi would be scattered (Gen. 49:7); it spread the knowledge of God through the land (every room was furnished with a candle); and it supported the ministers. He applies this to Christians today: those who are taught should share with their teachers. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/1Ch/1Ch_006.cfm
  - Jamieson‑Fausset‑Brown also mentions Jacob's prophecy, plus the need for teachers in every district. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-77.htm
  - Guzik says the Levites were "sprinkled" throughout the land of Israel by this arrangement. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/1-chronicles-4-8/
- **Cities of refuge: where views differ.**
  - Guzik (Pentecostal‑leaning list) sees the cities of refuge as a picture of Jesus. He adds a contrast: the cities protected only people innocent of murder, but Jesus takes in the guilty. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/numbers-35/
  - The Pulpit Commentary says one New Testament passage treats them as a picture of Christ's provision for the repentant sinner. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/1-chronicles-6.html
  - R. A. Watson (Expositor's Bible) disagrees. He says the manslayer is not a type of the sinner fleeing for his life from the justice of God, though he allows some points of illustration. https://ccel.org/ccel/watson_ra/expositornum/expositornum.xxvii.html
- **Modern and critical views.**
  - Watson calls the Levitical city law an ideal settlement, with no evidence that the command was ever fully carried out. Same URL.
  - Ellicott mentions the critical claim that the whole list rests on a historically false theory. He answers that Scripture never says only Levites lived in these cities. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
  - The Holman Bible Dictionary says the cities stayed under their tribes. It thinks the economic reason may have mattered most: the Levites had no steady income. https://www.studylight.org/dictionaries/eng/hbd/l/levitical-cities.html

**Verse by verse**

- **v. 55:** Joshua's wording is "the city of Arba… that is, Hebron," and "hill‑country" where Chronicles has "land." The word translated "pasturelands" (*migrashim*) means common grazing land, as opposed to fields for crops. Numbers 35:3–5 sets how far it extended. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **v. 56:** The Pulpit Commentary says this verse is the same as Joshua 21:12. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/1-chronicles-6.html Coffman (writing on Joshua) thinks Caleb probably agreed gladly to Hebron going to the priests, and kept the outlying fields. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/21-15.html
- **v. 57:** The Hebrew says "cities of refuge" in the plural. Keil & Delitzsch call this incorrect, because only Hebron was a city of refuge. Joshua 21:13 has the singular. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-57.htm The Cambridge Bible places Libnah in southwest Judah and Eshtemoa south of Hebron. Same URL. The Geneva Bible's note explains a refuge city as a place where a man who had killed someone could flee until his case was tried. Same URL.
- **v. 58:** Joshua calls Hilen "Holon," and some manuscripts read "Hilez." https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62613/ A Bible Hub article treats Hilen and Debir as supporting towns around Hebron, and connects the arrangement to Christ as Refuge (Heb. 6:18). https://biblehub.com/q/1_Chronicles_6_58_s_role_in_Levitical_cities.htm
- **vv. 59–60:** The Hebrew lists only 11 cities but gives a total of 13. Gill says Juttah and Gibeon dropped out through want of care in transcribing. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-57.htm The BSB fills them in from Joshua. The Pulpit Commentary also supplies them from Joshua, and notes that Joshua calls Ashan "Ain" and Alemeth "Almon." https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/1-chronicles-6.html Gibeon was where the tabernacle stood under David and Solomon. Anathoth was Jeremiah's hometown. https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm Alemeth is probably modern Khirbet Almit. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary
- **v. 61:** Verses 61–63 match Joshua 21:5–7. They give only the number of cities for each Levite group. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html According to Joshua, the ten Kohathite cities came from Ephraim, Manasseh and Dan, not Manasseh alone. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62613/
- **v. 62:** All the Gershonite cities were in the northern tribes, and two of them were cities of refuge. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary
- **v. 63:** The Merarites got four cities from each of Reuben, Gad and Zebulun. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **vv. 64–65:** Ellicott says the "cities" in v. 64 are the ones counted in vv. 61–63, as in Joshua 21:8. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **vv. 66–67:** The Hebrew again says "cities of refuge: Shechem, Gezer." The NIV corrects this from Joshua 21:21. https://www.blueletterbible.org/niv/1ch/6/61/s_344061 Bible Hub notes ruins on nearby Mount Gerizim that suggest Shechem stayed a sacred site. https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm Utley, citing Unger, says Gezer was one of the cities Israel did not control until the united monarchy (Saul, David and Solomon). https://bible.org/seriespage/joshua-21
- **vv. 68–69:** Ellicott thinks it fitting that Beth‑horon, Gibeon and Aijalon went to the sacred tribe. These were where God gave victory over the five Amorite kings. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html
- **v. 70:** "Bileam" is the Hebrew spelling of the name Balaam. Ellicott says it should read Ibleam, as the Greek Old Testament (Septuagint) does. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html Keil & Delitzsch say Chronicles is correct here, and that Joshua 21:25's names come from a copyist's error. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kdo/1-chronicles-6.html
- **v. 71:** Golan, in the later district of Gaulanitis east of the Sea of Galilee, was a city of refuge. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/1-chronicles-6.html Coffman says Joshua's "Beeshterah" is a short form of Beth‑Ashtaroth, so it is the same city as Ashtaroth. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/joshua-21.html
- **v. 72:** Joshua calls this Kedesh "Kishion." https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary Daberath is placed at modern Daburiyya, on the western slope of Mount Tabor. https://biblehub.com/q/1_Chr_6_72_s_link_to_Levitical_cities.htm
- **v. 73:** Keil & Delitzsch match Ramoth with Jarmuth/Remeth and Anem with En‑gannim in Joshua. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/21-13.html
- **vv. 74–75:** Abdon is modern Khirbet Abdeh. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary Keil & Delitzsch treat "Hukok" (for Joshua's Helkath) as a faulty reading. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/21-35.html
- **v. 76:** Keil & Delitzsch say Hammon is Joshua's Hammoth‑dor, and Kartan is a shortened form of Kiriathaim. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/21-15.html Kartan was near the Sea of Galilee. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary
- **v. 77:** "The rest of the Levites" simply means the Merarites are the group still left to list. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-77.htm Joshua lists four cities here (Jokneam, Kartah, Dimnah, Nahalal). Chronicles has two, and the first two names may have fallen out. Same URL.
  - The Cambridge Bible says Joshua is right about the number. Only a mountain called Tabor is clearly known from Old Testament times, though a town existed on it by 218 BC. Same URL.
  - Keil & Delitzsch think Rimmono is a better reading than Joshua's Dimnah. Same URL.
  - Gill suggests Tabor may be Chisloth‑tabor. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/joshua/21-35.html
  - The NIV adds Jokneam and Kartah from the Septuagint. https://www.blueletterbible.org/niv/1ch/6/61/s_344061
  - Bible Hub links Tabor to the traditional site of the Transfiguration. https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6-77.htm
- **vv. 78–79:** Bezer was a city of refuge (Deut. 4:43). "East of the Jordan" makes clear what "the other side Jordan" means. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/1_chronicles/6-77.htm Mephaath was in Reuben's territory. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary
- **vv. 80–81:** Ramoth was a city of refuge, and Mahanaim means "two camps." https://biblehub.com/1_chronicles/6.htm Coffman notes that each Levite group received at least one refuge city; the Merarites got two, Bezer and Ramoth‑Gilead. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/joshua-21.html
